briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Tensions in the Middle East have significantly escalated, with the US and Israel reportedly preparing for renewed military action against Iran following stalled negotiations. This comes amid increased Hezbollah operations in southern Lebanon, resulting in the death of an Israeli officer, and an Israeli airstrike killing a senior Hamas military commander in Gaza. Iran has responded with strong warnings against further aggression and announced a new mechanism for controlling maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz.

IRAN
Military operations in and against Iran are highly anticipated. The New York Times reports that the US and Israel are preparing for potential renewed military attacks, with President Trump explicitly stating, "This was the calm before the storm" and "no games!" The US has allowed a sanctions waiver for Russian oil to expire, in part to reduce reliance on the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Parliament Speaker Qalibaf asserted that Iran's 70-day resistance has accelerated a global shift, and Parliament's National Security Committee Chairman Ebrahim Azizi announced a new mechanism for the Strait of Hormuz. This mechanism will involve a "designated route" for cooperating commercial ships and will collect "essential charges" for specialized services, with payments for maritime cargo insurance through Bitcoin. Iran's Deputy Vice President stated that enemy military equipment would no longer be allowed through the Strait of Hormuz. A large MK-84 bomb was safely neutralized underground in Delfan, western Iran, after six days of excavation. A fire broke out at an oil factory in Maragheh, northwestern Iran, but was contained with no casualties. Kazakhstan delivered 30 wagons of humanitarian aid, including food and medical supplies, to Iran on May 16, 2026. Internally, Iran's Sima (state TV) featured programs with presenters brandishing weapons and demonstrating their use, interpreting this as preparation for potential ground invasion. State media also reported the confiscation of assets from 51 individuals in Yazd province on charges of "treason" and "cooperation with the enemy." Economically, the Tehran Stock Exchange is set to reopen on Tuesday, May 20, 2026, for the first time since "the war" began in late February. The Strait of Hormuz situation has caused an "inflationary shock" and increased Brent crude oil prices to $108.31 per barrel.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations included strikes on approximately 100 Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon over the weekend, encompassing surveillance posts, weapon depots, and terror infrastructure in areas including Tyre. The Israeli Air Force (IAF) killed two Hezbollah operatives at a rocket-launching site in southern Lebanon and successfully intercepted several rockets and two hostile drones launched by Hezbollah. In Gaza, the IDF killed Izz al-Din al-Haddad, the chief of Hamas's military wing and a planner of the October 7, 2023, attacks, along with his wife and daughter in Gaza City. The IDF also announced the killing of two Hamas terrorists, Khamer Iyad Muhammad Al-Matouq and Khaled Muhammad Salem Jouda, who had infiltrated Israel on October 7 and recently posed an immediate threat in northern Gaza, as well as Abdel Rahman Mahmoud Jumaa Shafi from Hamas's Bureij Battalion in central Gaza.
Casualties include Cpt. Maoz Israel Recanati, 24, a platoon commander in the Golani Brigade's 12th Battalion from Itamar, who was killed in a Hezbollah explosive drone attack in southern Lebanon on Friday, May 16, 2026. He is the seventh IDF soldier killed in southern Lebanon since a ceasefire began and the 20th since hostilities escalated in the "Iran war."
Home front air defense systems intercepted suspicious aerial targets and hostile aircraft, triggering sirens in northern communities such as Misgav Am and Metula. False alarms were also reported. A large explosion occurred at the state-owned Tomer rocket propulsion facility near Beit Shemesh, which develops and manufactures rocket engines for systems like Arrow 2/3 and Barak 8. Conflicting reports emerged regarding whether it was a controlled test, with local media questioning the official explanation due to the explosion's size and lack of prior public notification.
Politically, there's internal debate regarding a bill to split the Attorney General's role. Separately, the chairman of the Knesset Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee, Boaz Bismut, criticized the military's decision to imprison a Nahal soldier for 30 days for wearing a "Messiah patch," calling it disproportionate.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli forces conducted raids, killing a Palestinian man in the Jenin refugee camp. In Gaza City, a mass wedding took place for dozens of Palestinian couples whose marriages were delayed by war and displacement. Humanitarian efforts were also noted.
Regarding ceasefire negotiations, Hamas official Osama Hamdan stated in an Al Jazeera interview that the organization would not disarm, viewing it as a demand for surrender. He warned of a natural, regional, and wider Palestinian response if Israel continued its escalation. The killing of Izz al-Din al-Haddad was condemned by Iran and Hezbollah, with Hezbollah describing it as a violation of a standing ceasefire. A report highlighted Israeli authorities using military infrastructure to expand illegal settlements in the West Bank.

LEBANON
Hezbollah significantly escalated operations, launching several rockets and explosive drones at IDF troops in southern Lebanon overnight and during the day. An apparent Hezbollah drone triggered sirens in Metula and was intercepted. Two Hezbollah drones were shot down over southern Lebanon, while rockets and mortars were also fired, landing near IDF forces without causing injuries. Hezbollah claimed at least 19 military operations against Israeli positions, troops, and equipment over the past 24 hours. Attack drones were used to target an Israeli Humvee, Merkava tank in Al-Bayada, and armored personnel carriers in Bint Jbeil.
In response, the IDF conducted airstrikes on approximately 100 Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon over the weekend, including surveillance posts, weapon depots, and other terror infrastructure, with some strikes reaching the Tyre area. Two Hezbollah operatives were killed at a rocket-launching site following a rocket attack on IDF troops. Israeli artillery shells targeted the outskirts of Meifdoun, and airstrikes occurred near the Lebanese-Italian Hospital in Haouch and Deir Qanoun. These Israeli actions were reported by Press TV to have occurred despite a 45-day extension of a ceasefire agreement between Beirut and Tel Aviv.

SYRIA & IRAQ
In Syria, multiple explosions were reported near Izraa in Daraa province and in the Damascus countryside. Israeli occupation forces conducted ground incursions into Quneitra province, ransacking houses. In Iraq, a drone attack targeted Iranian Kurdish opposition sites in Sulaymaniyah province. A senior official of Iraqi Hezbollah Brigades, Mohammed Baqer al-Saadi, was arrested in Turkey and extradited to the US. He faces charges related to orchestrating at least 18 attacks in Europe, the US, and Canada since late February, allegedly in response to US-Israeli actions against Iran. These attacks include an attempted synagogue firebombing in Belgium and a planned attack on a Bank of America branch in Paris, attributed to the "Ashab al-Yamin" group, now linked to Iraqi Hezbollah Brigades. The Iraqi Parliament has requested the Foreign Ministry to intervene internationally regarding al-Saadi's transfer to the US. US refueling aircraft were observed operating over Anbar province, western Iraq, originating from Ben Gurion airport.

GULF STATES
Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan discussed regional developments, including the US-Iran ceasefire and de-escalation efforts, with Qatar's Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani. Saudi Arabia also declared a ban on political and religious slogans and flags during Hajj ceremonies in Mecca and Medina. The Trump administration is reportedly encouraging the UAE to deepen its involvement in the Iran war, including a suggestion to seize Iran's strategic Lavan Island in the Gulf. Kuwait's Defense Force declared its units at the highest level of defensive readiness and urged citizens to avoid suspicious objects potentially from Iranian attacks. Iran's First Vice President Mokhber warned Gulf states against serving US interests, particularly for hosting CENTCOM assets, stating that Iranian "restraint is not permanent." Oil prices jumped to over $109 per barrel due to the Strait of Hormuz situation, contributing to global economic fallout. A Qatari liquefied natural gas tanker docked in Karachi after traversing the Strait of Hormuz.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1. President Trump issued explicit threats, stating "This was the calm before the storm" and confirming his "patience is exhausted" regarding Iran, with US and Israel reportedly preparing for renewed military action.
2. Cpt. Maoz Israel Recanati, 24, an IDF officer, was killed in a Hezbollah explosive drone attack in southern Lebanon, making him the seventh IDF soldier killed in southern Lebanon since a ceasefire began.
3. The IDF confirmed the assassination of Izz al-Din al-Haddad, Hamas's military wing commander and an October 7 planner, along with his wife and daughter, in an airstrike in Gaza City.
4. Mohammed Baqer al-Saadi, a senior Iraqi Hezbollah Brigades official, was arrested in Turkey and extradited to the US, facing terrorism charges for allegedly planning attacks in Europe and the US.
5. Iran announced a new mechanism for the Strait of Hormuz, which includes charging tolls and requiring commercial ships to use a "designated route," with payments for maritime cargo insurance facilitated via Bitcoin.
6. A large explosion occurred at Israel’s state-owned Tomer rocket propulsion facility near Beit Shemesh, prompting conflicting reports on its nature and raising questions about its cause.
7. The US allowed a sanctions waiver for the purchase of Russian oil to expire, a decision linked to efforts to mitigate the economic impact of the Strait of Hormuz situation.
8. Iran's First Vice President Mokhber issued a stern warning to Gulf states, indicating that Iran's "restraint" for hosting US military assets would not be permanent.
9. Trump administration officials are reportedly encouraging the UAE to consider seizing Iran's Lavan Island to deepen its role in the conflict.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The risk of escalation is critically high, driven by the explicit threats from President Trump and reports of US-Israeli preparations for renewed military action against Iran. Active flashpoints include southern Lebanon, where Hezbollah's continuous attacks and the recent death of an IDF officer signal ongoing intense hostilities. The Strait of Hormuz is another critical flashpoint, with Iran's announcement of a new control mechanism, including tolls and a "designated route," directly challenging international maritime norms and posing a significant risk of confrontation. Kuwait's heightened defensive readiness and Iran's warnings to Gulf states underscore the regional tension. Iran's state media broadcasting weapon training and its "maximum reciprocal pressure" strategy indicate a preparedness for a multi-layered response to any aggression, including a potential ban on enemy military equipment passing through Hormuz. These developments suggest a fragile and volatile environment where miscalculation could rapidly lead to broader conflict.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The US posture, as articulated by President Trump, is one of heightened aggression, with explicit threats against Iran and the White House issuing a warning: "If you harm Americans... we will find and kill you." Trump's recent visit to China reportedly yielded no strategic gains regarding Iran. The US allowed a sanctions waiver for Russian oil to expire, contributing to market shifts and signaling continued economic pressure.
Gulf states are responding with caution and concern. Qatar and Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministers engaged in discussions focused on de-escalation and regional developments. Kuwait's Defense Force units are at their highest defensive readiness, and Saudi Arabia has banned political slogans during Hajj. The UAE is reportedly being pressured by the Trump administration to deepen its involvement in the Iran conflict, including the potential seizure of Lavan Island.
European nations are grappling with the broader geopolitical instability. Josep Borrell, a former senior EU official, critiqued the EU's perceived weakness on the global stage. France has offered to assist Ukraine with anti-ballistic missile development, reflecting ongoing concerns about regional security.
Russia has openly opposed a US resolution regarding the Strait of Hormuz, echoing China's stance, and its representative to international organizations warned against US-Israeli "strategic mistakes" in potentially renewing attacks on Iran. Russia has also taken steps to integrate Transnistria residents by fast-tracking Russian citizenship.
China's response to the escalating tensions has been largely non-committal regarding cooperation with the US on Iran, as evidenced by President Trump's unfruitful visit. However, the Chinese Commerce Ministry confirmed arrangements with the US for aircraft purchases and parts.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several reports contain contradictions and unverified claims. The significant explosion at the Tomer rocket propulsion facility near Beit Shemesh was initially labeled a "controlled test" by Israeli sources, but other media questioned this narrative, citing the scale of the blast and absence of pre-notification to emergency services. This suggests a potential information control effort by Israeli authorities. There are conflicting references to a "ceasefire" – sometimes linked to US-Iran, other times to Israel-Lebanon – with reports of Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon occurring *despite* an extended ceasefire, indicating that the terms or adherence to any such agreement are unclear or being violated.

Unverified claims include Omid Dana's report that President Trump explicitly threatened Speaker Qalibaf with assassination during a Fox News interview, calling him "Mohammad something," which requires independent confirmation. Similarly, the claim regarding Pavel Durov (Telegram CEO) making geopolitical comments about Dubai traffic and Iranian "fireworks" lacks robust verification. Claims about Iranian officials possibly fleeing to Moscow due to security concerns also remain unverified.

Propaganda indicators are evident across multiple sources. Iranian state media emphasize themes of "resistance," the rise of the "Global South," and condemn "Western imperialism," utilizing strong nationalistic imagery like the Sima weapon training broadcasts, some of which appear to target the UAE. Trump's social media posts are clearly designed to project an image of decisive strength and threat. Certain channels like "omid dana" often present highly opinionated and sensationalized content, employing derogatory terms and making speculative predictions about regime collapse.

Key reporting gaps include a lack of precise details on the nature and scope of the "US-Iran ceasefire" mentioned by Qatari and Saudi officials. The exact implications of the "Iran war" as referenced in relation to IDF casualties are also not fully elaborated, leaving it ambiguous whether this refers to a declared war or prolonged, escalated hostilities. A clearer understanding of the official Israeli stance on the Beit Shemesh explosion and specific details of any ceasefire violations would be beneficial. The full context and implications of the alleged US pressure on the UAE to seize Lavan Island also require further information.
